NKJV.1: A good name is better than precious ointment, And the day of death than the day of one’s birth;
NKJV.2: Better to go to the house of mourning Than to go to the house of feasting, For that is the end of all men; And the living will take it to heart.
NKJV.3: Sorrow is better than laughter, For by a sad countenance the heart is made better.
NKJV.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, But the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
NKJV.5: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise Than for a man to hear the song of fools.
NKJV.6: For like the crackling of thorns under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
NKJV.7: Surely oppression destroys a wise man’s reason, And a bribe debases the heart.
NKJV.8: The end of a thing is better than its beginning; The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
NKJV.9: Do not hasten in your spirit to be angry, For anger rests in the bosom of fools.
NKJV.10: Do not say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not inquire wisely concerning this.
NKJV.11: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, And profitable to those who see the sun.
NKJV.12: For wisdom is a defense as money is a defense, But the excellence of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who have it.
NKJV.13: Consider the work of God; For who can make straight what He has made crooked?
NKJV.14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, But in the day of adversity consider: Surely God has appointed the one as well as the other, So that man can find out nothing that will come after him.
NKJV.15: I have seen everything in my days of vanity: There is a just man who perishes in his righteousness, And there is a wicked man who prolongs life in his wickedness.
NKJV.16: Do not be overly righteous,  Nor be overly wise: Why should you destroy yourself?
NKJV.17: Do not be overly wicked, Nor be foolish:  Why should you die before your time?
NKJV.18: It is good that you grasp this, And also not remove your hand from the other; For he who fears God will escape them all.
NKJV.19: Wisdom strengthens the wise More than ten rulers of the city.
NKJV.20: For there is not a just man on earth who does good And does not sin.
NKJV.21: Also do not take to heart everything people say, Lest you hear your servant cursing you.
NKJV.22: For many times, also, your own heart has known That even you have cursed others.
NKJV.23: All this I have proved by wisdom. I said, “I will be wise”; But it was far from me.
NKJV.24: As for that which is far off and exceedingly deep, Who can find it out?
NKJV.25: I applied my heart to know, To search and seek out wisdom and the reason of things, To know the wickedness of folly, Even of foolishness and madness.
NKJV.26: And I find more bitter than death The woman whose heart is snares and nets, Whose hands are fetters. He who pleases God shall escape from her, But the sinner shall be trapped by her.
NKJV.27: Here is what I have found,” says the Preacher, “Adding one thing to the other to find out the reason,
NKJV.28: Which my soul still seeks but I cannot find:  One man among a thousand I have found, But a woman among all these I have not found.
NKJV.29: Truly, this only I have found:  That God made man upright, But they have sought out many schemes.”

NASB.1: A good name is better than a good ointment, And the day of [one's] death is better than the day of one's birth.
NASB.2: It is better to go to a house of mourning Than to go to a house of feasting, Because that is the end of every man, And the living takes [it] to heart.
NASB.3: Sorrow is better than laughter, For when a face is sad a heart may be happy.
NASB.4: The mind of the wise is in the house of mourning, While the mind of fools is in the house of pleasure.
NASB.5: It is better to listen to the rebuke of a wise man Than for one to listen to the song of fools.
NASB.6: For as the crackling of thorn bushes under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool; And this too is futility.
NASB.7: For oppression makes a wise man mad, And a bribe corrupts the heart.
NASB.8: The end of a matter is better than its beginning; Patience of spirit is better than haughtiness of spirit.
NASB.9: Do not be eager in your heart to be angry, For anger resides in the bosom of fools.
NASB.10: Do not say, 'Why is it that the former days were better than these?' For it is not from wisdom that you ask about this.
NASB.11: Wisdom along with an inheritance is good And an advantage to those who see the sun.
NASB.12: For wisdom is protection [just as] money is protection, But the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the lives of its possessors.
NASB.13: Consider the work of God, For who is able to straighten what He has bent?
NASB.14: In the day of prosperity be happy, But in the day of adversity consider-- God has made the one as well as the other So that man will not discover anything [that will be] after him.
NASB.15: I have seen everything during my lifetime of futility; there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness and there is a wicked man who prolongs [his life] in his wickedness.
NASB.16: Do not be excessively righteous and do not be overly wise. Why should you ruin yourself?
NASB.17: Do not be excessively wicked and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
NASB.18: It is good that you grasp one thing and also not let go of the other; for the one who fears God comes forth with both of them.
NASB.19: Wisdom strengthens a wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
NASB.20: Indeed, there is not a righteous man on earth who [continually] does good and who never sins.
NASB.21: Also, do not take seriously all words which are spoken, so that you will not hear your servant cursing you.
NASB.22: For you also have realized that you likewise have many times cursed others.
NASB.23: I tested all this with wisdom, [and] I said, 'I will be wise,' but it was far from me.
NASB.24: What has been is remote and exceedingly mysterious. Who can discover it?
NASB.25: I directed my mind to know, to investigate and to seek wisdom and an explanation, and to know the evil of folly and the foolishness of madness.
NASB.26: And I discovered more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are chains. One who is pleasing to God will escape from her, but the sinner will be captured by her.
NASB.27: 'Behold, I have discovered this,' says the Preacher, '[adding] one thing to another to find an explanation,
NASB.28: which I am still seeking but have not found. I have found one man among a thousand, but I have not found a woman among all these.
NASB.29: 'Behold, I have found only this, that God made men upright, but they have sought out many devices.'

ESV.1: A good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of birth.
ESV.2: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for this is the end of all mankind, and the living will lay it to heart.
ESV.3: Sorrow is better than laughter, for by sadness of face the heart is made glad.
ESV.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
ESV.5: It is better for a man to hear the rebuke of the wise than to hear the song of fools.
ESV.6: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fools; this also is vanity.
ESV.7: Surely oppression drives the wise into madness, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
ESV.8: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning, and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
ESV.9: Be not quick in your spirit to become angry, for anger lodges in the heart  of fools.
ESV.10: Say not, “Why were the former days better than these?” For it is not from wisdom that you ask this.
ESV.11: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, an advantage to those who see the sun.
ESV.12: For the protection of wisdom is like the protection of money, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
ESV.13: Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?
ESV.14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other, so that man may not find out anything that will be after him.
ESV.15: In my vain  life I have seen everything. There is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who prolongs his life in his evildoing.
ESV.16: Be not overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
ESV.17: Be not overly wicked, neither be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
ESV.18: It is good that you should take hold of this, and from that withhold not your hand, for the one who fears God shall come out from both of them.
ESV.19: Wisdom gives strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
ESV.20: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
ESV.21: Do not take to heart all the things that people say, lest you hear your servant cursing you.
ESV.22: Your heart knows that many times you yourself have cursed others.
ESV.23: All this I have tested by wisdom. I said, “I will be wise,” but it was far from me.
ESV.24: That which has been is far off, and deep, very deep; who can find it out?
ESV.25: I turned my heart to know and to search out and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know the wickedness of folly and the foolishness that is madness.
ESV.26: And I find something more bitter than death: the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and whose hands are fetters. He who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is taken by her.
ESV.27: Behold, this is what I found, says the Preacher, while adding one thing to another to find the scheme of things —
ESV.28: which my soul has sought repeatedly, but I have not found. One man among a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
ESV.29: See, this alone I found, that God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes.

NLT.1:
A good reputation is more valuable than costly perfume.
And the day you die is better than the day you are born.
NLT.2:
Better to spend your time at funerals than at parties.
After all, everyone dies —
so the living should take this to heart.
NLT.3:
Sorrow is better than laughter,
for sadness has a refining influence on us.
NLT.4:
A wise person thinks a lot about death,
while a fool thinks only about having a good time.
NLT.5:
Better to be criticized by a wise person
than to be praised by a fool.
NLT.6:
A fool’s laughter is quickly gone,
like thorns crackling in a fire.
This also is meaningless.
NLT.7:
Extortion turns wise people into fools,
and bribes corrupt the heart.
NLT.8:
Finishing is better than starting.
Patience is better than pride.
NLT.9:
Control your temper,
for anger labels you a fool.
NLT.10:
Don’t long for “the good old days.”
This is not wise.
NLT.11:
Wisdom is even better when you have money.
Both are a benefit as you go through life.
NLT.12:
Wisdom and money can get you almost anything,
but only wisdom can save your life.
NLT.13:
Accept the way God does things,
for who can straighten what he has made crooked?
NLT.14:
Enjoy prosperity while you can,
but when hard times strike, realize that both come from God.
Remember that nothing is certain in this life.
NLT.15: I have seen everything in this meaningless life, including the death of good young people and the long life of wicked people.
NLT.16: So don’t be too good or too wise! Why destroy yourself?
NLT.17: On the other hand, don’t be too wicked either. Don’t be a fool! Why die before your time?
NLT.18: Pay attention to these instructions, for anyone who fears God will avoid both extremes.
NLT.19: One wise person is stronger than ten leading citizens of a town!
NLT.20: Not a single person on earth is always good and never sins.
NLT.21: Don’t eavesdrop on others — you may hear your servant curse you.
NLT.22: For you know how often you yourself have cursed others.
NLT.23: I have always tried my best to let wisdom guide my thoughts and actions. I said to myself, “I am determined to be wise.” But it didn’t work.
NLT.24: Wisdom is always distant and difficult to find.
NLT.25: I searched everywhere, determined to find wisdom and to understand the reason for things. I was determined to prove to myself that wickedness is stupid and that foolishness is madness.
NLT.26: I discovered that a seductive woman is a trap more bitter than death. Her passion is a snare, and her soft hands are chains. Those who are pleasing to God will escape her, but sinners will be caught in her snare.
NLT.27: “This is my conclusion,” says the Teacher. “I discovered this after looking at the matter from every possible angle.
NLT.28: Though I have searched repeatedly, I have not found what I was looking for. Only one out of a thousand men is virtuous, but not one woman!
NLT.29: But I did find this: God created people to be virtuous, but they have each turned to follow their own downward path.”

AMP.1:
A good name is better than precious perfume,
And the day of one's death better than the day of one's birth.
AMP.2:
It is better to go to the house of mourning
Than to go to the house of feasting,
For that [day of death] is the end of every man,
And the living will take it to heart and solemnly ponder its meaning.
AMP.3:
Sorrow is better than laughter,
For when a face is sad (deep in thought) the heart may be happy [because it is growing in wisdom].
AMP.4:
The heart of the wise [learns when it] is in the house of mourning,
But the heart of fools is [senseless] in the house of pleasure.
AMP.5:
It is better to listen to the rebuke of the wise man and pursue wisdom
Than for one to listen to the song of fools and pursue stupidity.
AMP.6:
For like the crackling of [burning] thorn bushes under a pot,
So is the laughter of the fool;
And this too is vanity (futility).
AMP.7:
For oppression makes a wise man foolish,
And a bribe corrupts the [good judgment of the] heart.
AMP.8:
The end of a matter is better than its beginning;
Patience of spirit is better than haughtiness of spirit (pride).
AMP.9:
Do not be eager in your heart to be angry,
For anger dwells in the heart of fools.
AMP.10:
Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?"
For it is not from wisdom that you ask about this.
AMP.11:
Wisdom along with an inheritance is good
And an [excellent] advantage for those who see the sun.
AMP.12:
For wisdom is a protection even as money is a protection,
But the [excellent] advantage of knowledge is that wisdom shields and preserves the lives of its possessors.
AMP.13:
Consider the work of God:
Who can make straight what He has bent?
AMP.14:
In the day of prosperity be joyful,
But in the day of adversity consider that
God has made the one as well as the other,
So that man will not find out anything that will be after him.
AMP.15: I have seen everything during my [fleeting] days of futility; there is a righteous man who perishes in [spite of] his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives a long life in [spite of] his wickedness.
AMP.16: Do not be excessively righteous [like those given to self-conceit], and do not be overly wise (pretentious)—why should you bring yourself to ruin?
AMP.17: Do not be excessively or willfully wicked and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
AMP.18: It is good that you take hold of one thing (righteousness) and also not let go of the other (wisdom); for the one who fears and worships God [with awe-filled reverence] will come forth with both of them.
AMP.19: Wisdom strengthens the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
AMP.20: Indeed, there is not a righteous man on earth who always does good and who never sins.
AMP.21: Also, do not take seriously everything that is said, so that you will not hear your servant cursing you,
AMP.22: for you also know that you too have cursed others many times.
AMP.23: I have tested all this with wisdom. I said, "I will be wise [independently of God]," but true wisdom was far from me.
AMP.24: Whatever has been is far off, deeply remote and exceedingly mysterious. Who can discover it [for it is beyond the grasp of man]?
AMP.25: I turned around and directed my heart to know, to investigate and to seek [skillful and godly] wisdom and the reason for things, and to know that wickedness is folly and that foolishness is madness [leading to stupidity and recklessness].
AMP.26: And I discovered that [of all irrational sins none has been so destructive in beguiling one away from God as immoral women for] more bitter than death is the woman whose heart is [composed of] snares and nets, and whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God will escape from her, but the sinner will be taken captive by her [evil].
AMP.27: "Behold, I have discovered this," says the Preacher, "while adding one thing to another to find an explanation,
AMP.28: which I am still seeking but have not found. I have found one man among a thousand [who pleases God], but I have not found [such] a woman among all these [a thousand in my harem].
AMP.29: Behold, I have found only this [as a reason]: God made man upright and uncorrupted, but they [both men and women] have sought out many devices [for evil]."

WEB.1: A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
WEB.2: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
WEB.3: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
WEB.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
WEB.5: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
WEB.6: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
WEB.7: Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
WEB.8: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
WEB.9: Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
WEB.10: Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
WEB.11: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those who see the sun.
WEB.12: For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
WEB.13: Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?
WEB.14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
WEB.15: All this I have seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives long in his evildoing.
WEB.16: Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
WEB.17: Don’t be too wicked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
WEB.18: It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also from that don’t withdraw your hand; for he who fears God will come out of them all.
WEB.19: Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
WEB.20: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn’t sin.
WEB.21: Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you;
WEB.22: for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
WEB.23: All this I have proved in wisdom. I said, “I will be wise”; but it was far from me.
WEB.24: That which is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
WEB.25: I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
WEB.26: I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner will be ensnared by her.
WEB.27: “Behold, I have found this,” says the Preacher, “to one another, to find out the scheme;
WEB.28: which my soul still seeks; but I have not found. I have found one man among a thousand; but I have not found a woman among all those.
WEB.29: Behold, I have only found this: that God made man upright; but they search for many schemes.”

MSG.1:
A good reputation is better than a fat bank account.
Your death date tells more than your birth date.
MSG.2:
You learn more at a funeral than at a feast—
After all, that's where we'll end up. We might discover
something from it.
MSG.3:
Crying is better than laughing.
It blotches the face but it scours the heart.
MSG.4:
Sages invest themselves in hurt and grieving.
Fools waste their lives in fun and games.
MSG.5:
You'll get more from the rebuke of a sage
Than from the song and dance of fools.
MSG.6:
The giggles of fools are like the crackling of twigs
Under the cooking pot. And like smoke.
MSG.7:
Brutality stupefies even the wise
And destroys the strongest heart.
MSG.8:
Endings are better than beginnings.
Sticking to it is better than standing out.
MSG.9:
Don't be quick to fly off the handle.
Anger boomerangs. You can spot a fool by the lumps on his head.
MSG.10:
Don't always be asking, "Where are the good old days?"
Wise folks don't ask questions like that.
MSG.11:
Wisdom is better when it's paired with money,
Especially if you get both while you're still living.
MSG.12:
Double protection: wisdom and wealth!
Plus this bonus: Wisdom energizes its owner.
MSG.13:
Take a good look at God's work.
Who could simplify and reduce Creation's curves and angles
To a plain straight line?
MSG.14:
On a good day, enjoy yourself;
On a bad day, examine your conscience.
God arranges for both kinds of days
So that we won't take anything for granted.
MSG.15: I've seen it all in my brief and pointless life—here a good person cut down in the middle of doing good, there a bad person living a long life of sheer evil.
MSG.16: So don't knock yourself out being good, and don't go overboard being wise. Believe me, you won't get anything out of it.
MSG.17: But don't press your luck by being bad, either. And don't be reckless. Why die needlessly?
MSG.18: It's best to stay in touch with both sides of an issue. A person who fears God deals responsibly with all of reality, not just a piece of it.
MSG.19:
Wisdom puts more strength in one wise person
Than ten strong men give to a city.
MSG.20:
There's not one totally good person on earth,
Not one who is truly pure and sinless.
MSG.21:
Don't eavesdrop on the conversation of others.
What if the gossip's about you and you'd rather not hear it?
MSG.22:
You've done that a few times, haven't you—said things
Behind someone's back you wouldn't say to his face?
MSG.23: I tested everything in my search for wisdom. I set out to be wise, but it was beyond me,
MSG.24: far beyond me, and deep—oh so deep! Does anyone ever find it?
MSG.25: I concentrated with all my might, studying and exploring and seeking wisdom—the meaning of life. I also wanted to identify evil and stupidity, foolishness and craziness.
MSG.26: One discovery: A woman can be a bitter pill to swallow, full of seductive scheming and grasping. The lucky escape her; the undiscerning get caught.
MSG.27: At least this is my experience—what I, the Quester, have pieced together as I've tried to make sense of life.
MSG.28: But the wisdom I've looked for I haven't found. I didn't find one man or woman in a thousand worth my while.
MSG.29: Yet I did spot one ray of light in this murk: God made men and women true and upright; we're the ones who've made a mess of things.

NIV.1:
Wisdom
A good name is better than fine perfume,
and the day of death better than the day of birth.
NIV.2:
It is better to go to a house of mourning
than to go to a house of feasting,
for death is the destiny of every man;
the living should take this to heart.
NIV.3:
Sorrow is better than laughter,
because a sad face is good for the heart.
NIV.4:
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning,
but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
NIV.5:
It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke
than to listen to the song of fools.
NIV.6:
Like the crackling of thorns under the pot,
so is the laughter of fools.
This too is meaningless.
NIV.7:
Extortion turns a wise man into a fool,
and a bribe corrupts the heart.
NIV.8:
The end of a matter is better than its beginning,
and patience is better than pride.
NIV.9:
Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit,
for anger resides in the lap of fools.
NIV.10:
Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?”
For it is not wise to ask such questions.
NIV.11:
Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing
and benefits those who see the sun.
NIV.12:
Wisdom is a shelter
as money is a shelter,
but the advantage of knowledge is this:
that wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.
NIV.13:
Consider what God has done:
Who can straighten
what he has made crooked?
NIV.14:
When times are good, be happy;
but when times are bad, consider:
God has made the one
as well as the other.
Therefore, a man cannot discover
anything about his future.
NIV.15:
In this meaningless life of mine I have seen both of these:
a righteous man perishing in his righteousness,
and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
NIV.16:
Do not be overrighteous,
neither be overwise—
why destroy yourself?
NIV.17:
Do not be overwicked,
and do not be a fool—
why die before your time?
NIV.18:
It is good to grasp the one
and not let go of the other.
The man who fears God will avoid all extremes.
NIV.19:
Wisdom makes one wise man more powerful
than ten rulers in a city.
NIV.20:
There is not a righteous man on earth
who does what is right and never sins.
NIV.21:
Do not pay attention to every word people say,
or you may hear your servant cursing you—
NIV.22:
for you know in your heart
that many times you yourself have cursed others.
NIV.23:
All this I tested by wisdom and I said,
“I am determined to be wise”—
but this was beyond me.
NIV.24:
Whatever wisdom may be,
it is far off and most profound—
who can discover it?
NIV.25:
So I turned my mind to understand,
to investigate and to search out wisdom and the scheme of things
and to understand the stupidity of wickedness
and the madness of folly.
NIV.26:
I find more bitter than death
the woman who is a snare,
whose heart is a trap
and whose hands are chains.
The man who pleases God will escape her,
but the sinner she will ensnare.
NIV.27:
“Look,” says the Teacher, “this is what I have discovered:
“Adding one thing to another to discover the scheme of things—
NIV.28:
while I was still searching
but not finding—
I found one upright man among a thousand,
but not one upright woman among them all.
NIV.29:
This only have I found:
God made mankind upright,
but men have gone in search of many schemes.”

NET.1: A good reputation is better than precious perfume; likewise, the day of one’s death is better than the day of one’s birth.
NET.2: It is better to go to a funeral than a feast. For death is the destiny of every person, and the living should take this to heart.
NET.3: Sorrow is better than laughter, because sober reflection is good for the heart.
NET.4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of merrymaking.
NET.5: It is better for a person to receive a rebuke from those who are wise than to listen to the song of fools.
NET.6: For like the crackling of quick-burning thorns under a cooking pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This kind of folly also is useless.
NET.7: Surely oppression can turn a wise person into a fool; likewise, a bribe corrupts the heart.
NET.8: The end of a matter is better than its beginning; likewise, patience is better than pride.
NET.9: Do not let yourself be quickly provoked, for anger resides in the lap of fools.
NET.10: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these days?” for it is not wise to ask that.
NET.11: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is a good thing; it benefits those who see the light of day.
NET.12: For wisdom provides protection, just as money provides protection. But the advantage of knowledge is this: Wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
NET.13: Consider the work of God: For who can make straight what he has bent?
NET.14: In times of prosperity be joyful, but in times of adversity consider this: God has made one as well as the other, so that no one can discover what the future holds.
NET.15: During the days of my fleeting life I have seen both of these things: Sometimes a righteous person dies prematurely in spite of his righteousness, and sometimes a wicked person lives long in spite of his evil deeds.
NET.16: So do not be excessively righteous or excessively wise; otherwise you might be disappointed.
NET.17: Do not be excessively wicked and do not be a fool; otherwise you might die before your time.
NET.18: It is best to take hold of one warning without letting go of the other warning; for the one who fears God will follow both warnings.
NET.19: Wisdom gives a wise person more protection than ten rulers in a city.
NET.20: For there is not one truly righteous person on the earth who continually does good and never sins.
NET.21: Also, do not pay attention to everything that people say; otherwise, you might even hear your servant cursing you.
NET.22: For you know in your own heart that you also have cursed others many times.
NET.23: I have examined all this by wisdom; I said, “I am determined to comprehend this” — but it was beyond my grasp.
NET.24: Whatever has happened is beyond human understanding; it is far deeper than anyone can fathom.
NET.25: I tried to understand, examine, and comprehend the role of wisdom in the scheme of things, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the insanity of folly.
NET.26: I discovered this: More bitter than death is the kind of woman who is like a hunter’s snare; her heart is like a hunter’s net and her hands are like prison chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is captured by her.
NET.27: The Teacher says: I discovered this while trying to discover the scheme of things, item by item.
NET.28: What I have continually sought, I have not found; I have found only one upright man among a thousand, but I have not found one upright woman among all of them.
NET.29: This alone have I discovered: God made humankind upright, but they have sought many evil schemes.
